metadata.description:
Source-owned, non-secret provenance copied from the canonical document.
Code documents use this for repository and revision identity.

lexical_score.description:
Raw SQLite FTS5 score. Lower values are better; retained for
diagnostics and backwards-compatible clients.

relevance_score.description:
Bounded, higher-is-better score used to order native-memory recall.
This combines query coverage, lexical relevance, memory salience, and
freshness without contacting a provider or loading the corpus.

ConfiguredSourceStatus.description:
Safe, non-secret source configuration shared by the HTTP status API and the
MCP `brain_status` tool. This deliberately omits credential paths,
environment variable names, tokens, and connector arguments.

active.description: Active and currently valid memories available to recall.

expired.description:
Active records whose validity window has elapsed. They remain in the
store for export/audit history but are not eligible for recall.

complete.description:
Whether the validation covered the entire source within its limits.
`false` marks a bounded sample that may authorize only equally bounded
non-reconciling runs; `None` means the record's completeness is unknown
and cannot authorize recurring or full-corpus sync.

reduced_tokens.description: Tokens omitted by context budgeting and formatting overhead.

reduction_ratio.description: Bounded source-to-context reduction ratio in the range 0.0–1.0.

source_tokens.description:
Estimated tokens in the untruncated evidence/memory payload before
context budgeting. This is a size metric only; no content is emitted.

approval_required.description: A transport must call the explicit memory retain/remember operation.

oneOf.description: Use only the deterministic local implementation.

Try a configured provider, then return the deterministic result if it
is unavailable or returns an invalid/ungrounded response.

A provider is required; unavailable or failed providers return no
synthesized result and an explicit outcome.
